ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude on the side $BC$, $CE$ is the median on the side $AB$, $DG \perp CE$ at $G$, and $CD = AE$. Given that $BD = 6$, $CD = 5$, and $CG = EG$; find the area of $\triangle CDG$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $CE$ is the median of side $AB$,\\
hence $AE=BE$,\\
since $BD=6, CD=5$,\\
it follows that $AB=10$,\\
thus $AD=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=8$,\\
therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}\times 11\times 8=44$, the area of $\triangle ABD=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8=24$,\\
since $CE$ is the median of side $AB$,\\
it follows that the area of $\triangle BEC=\frac{1}{2}$ area of $\triangle ABC=22$,\\
since $DE$ is the median of side $AB$,\\
it follows that the area of $\triangle BDE=\frac{1}{2}$ area of $\triangle ABD=12$,\\
thus the area of $\triangle EDC$ is area of $\triangle BEC$ - area of $\triangle EDB=22-12=10$,\\
additionally, since $CG=EG$,\\
the area of $\triangle CDG=\frac{1}{2}$ area of $\triangle EDC=\boxed{5}$.

Therefore, the area of $\triangle ABC=\frac{1}{2}\times 11\times 8=44$, and the area of $\triangle ABD=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8=24$. Since $CE$ is the median of side $AB$, the area of $\triangle BEC=\frac{1}{2}$ the area of $\triangle ABC=22$. Since $DE$ is the median of side $AB$, the area of $\triangle BDE=\frac{1}{2}$ the area of $\triangle ABD=12$. Thus the area of $\triangle EDC$ is area of $\triangle BEC$ minus area of $\triangle EDB$, which is $22-12=10$. Additionally, since $CG=EG$, the area of $\triangle CDG=\frac{1}{2}$ the area of $\triangle EDC=\boxed{5}$.

Because CE is the median in triangle ABC from C to the midpoint E of AB, the area of triangle BEC is half the area of triangle ABC, namely 22. In triangle ABD, E is the midpoint of AB, so DE divides triangle ABD into two parts of equal area; therefore the area of triangle BDE is 24/2=12. Thus the area of triangle EDC is equal to the area of triangle BEC minus the area of triangle BDE, namely 22-12=10. Also because CG=EG, G is the midpoint of CE; in triangle EDC, DG divides the base EC into two equal segments CG and EG, and the two small triangles CDG and EDG share the altitude from D to CE, so their areas are equal. Therefore the area of triangle CDG is 10/2=5.
